steps.title: Apply online for your study permit (temporary resident visa included)
steps.why: Most foreign nationals need a study permit to study at a designated learning institution in Canada, and you should apply before you travel. Because your citizenship requires a visitor visa to enter Canada, IRCC issues the temporary resident visa together with your study permit approval — you don't apply separately or pay another fee, and the visa is placed in your passport showing single or multiple entry. Study permit processing times vary by country, so apply as early as possible; submitting an incomplete application (including missing biometrics or documents) causes further delays. If you're a doctoral (PhD) student, check whether you and accompanying family members qualify for faster processing.
prerequisites: An IRCC secure account (used to pay fees, submit the application, and check status)
A scanner or camera to create electronic copies of your documents
A valid credit or debit card
Your local visa office instructions for the country/territory you're applying from
The valid passport you'll travel with — the visa will be issued in it
Read the instruction guide and prepare answers for the online tool to generate your personalized document checklist
Plan for biometrics (fingerprints and photo)
steps.cost: CAN$150 study permit fee; no additional fee for the temporary resident visa issued with approval
steps.time_estimate: Processing times vary by country — apply well before your program start date

steps.title: Book and give your biometrics within 30 days of the BIL
steps.why: Biometrics (fingerprints and photo) confirm your identity and are required for most study permit applications. IRCC sends a biometrics instruction letter (BIL) after you submit your application, and you have 30 days to give them. Booking your collection appointment as soon as you can avoids processing delays — IRCC can't finalize your permit without them. Once given, your biometrics are valid for 10 years, making repeat trips to Canada easier.
prerequisites: Submitted study permit application online
Paid the biometrics fee at the time of application submission
Received your biometrics instruction letter (BIL) from IRCC
Valid passport/travel document to bring to the appointment
steps.cost: CAN$85 per individual applicant; maximum CAN$170 total for families applying at the same time (spouse/common-law partner and dependent children)
steps.time_estimate: Book immediately upon receiving the BIL — you must give biometrics within 30 days

steps.title: Arrange your international tuition payment early — check assessed fees in Workday, then start the transfer
steps.why: Your specific fees are assessed and shown under "Finances" in Workday, and Winter Session Term 1 tuition is due on a fixed date (September 9, 2026 on UBC's published financial schedule), with student fees included in that first instalment. Because you are paying from a restricted or less liquid currency corridor, there are fewer transfer providers, longer settlement times, and possible exchange-control paperwork on the sending side — so confirm the amount owing in Workday and begin the transfer well ahead of the due date rather than in the final week. Check both UBC's payment guidance and your home country's (or funding programme's) outbound-payment and proof-of-funds rules, since your funder may require its own documentation before releasing or remitting money. Budget for charges that appear on your account beyond tuition: as an international student, the temporary iMED medical insurance fee is charged to your account when you register for courses and covers you until BC Medical Services Plan (MSP) coverage begins (likely in November).
prerequisites: Accepted your offer of admission and paid the acceptance deposit ($3,000 for students on a study permit) through the Applicant Service Centre
Registered for courses so your fees are assessed
Access to Workday to view your assessed fees under "Finances"
steps.cost: Tuition and student fees vary — use UBC's cost estimator for a projection and Workday ("Finances") for your actual assessed amount; temporary iMED insurance is $237 (or $338 for one-term exchange students) plus a $10.54 direct billing fee. Add your bank's or provider's transfer and currency-conversion charges.
steps.time_estimate: 1–2 hours to confirm amounts and set up the payment, plus several weeks of lead time before the due date for the transfer to clear

steps.title: Prepare your port-of-entry documents for arrival in Canada
steps.why: Your approval isn't your study permit — the port of entry letter of introduction is. A border services officer issues your actual study permit on arrival, using the permit reference number in that letter, and will confirm you meet basic entry requirements. Having every document in your carry-on prevents delays or refusal of entry.
prerequisites: Approved study permit application and port of entry letter of introduction received in your online account
Valid passport — the same one you used to apply for your study permit
Valid eTA (linked to that passport) or visitor visa in your passport, if you need one; or valid green card plus passport of nationality if you're a US lawful permanent resident
Copy of your valid UBC letter of acceptance (an updated LOA plus valid letter of introduction if you deferred your enrolment)
Letters of reference or any other documents the visa office told you to bring
Proof of enough money for your stay
steps.time_estimate: 1–2 hours to gather documents before departure

steps.title: Apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN) online with Service Canada
steps.why: A SIN is the 9-digit Service Canada number you need to start working in Canada, file taxes, and access government programs — and you must give it to UBC for tax purposes. If you'll be a TA or RA, apply as soon as you've arrived and have your study permit: online applications take up to 5 business days, mail up to 20 business days, while an in-person appointment issues the SIN during your visit. International students receive a SIN starting with "9", indicating temporary resident status.
prerequisites: Arrive in Canada and receive your study permit at the airport or border crossing — international students can only apply after arrival

Check that your study permit carries a work condition, e.g. "May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186(f), (v) or (w)...", "May work 24 hours per week off campus or full time during regular breaks...", or "May accept employment on the campus of the institution at which registered in full-time studies" — if it has no work condition, apply to change your study permit conditions first
Have your study or work permit and a copy of your passport ready; translate any document not in English or French
Confirm you are otherwise eligible to work in Canada — a SIN alone is not enough
After you receive it, add your SIN in Workday and keep it protected as sensitive personal information
steps.time_estimate: Up to 5 business days online; up to 20 business days by mail; same-visit if applying in person

steps.title: Apply for BC Medical Services Plan (MSP) as soon as you arrive in B.C.
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP) so you can access provincial health benefits like doctor visits. If you're new to Canada, apply as soon as you arrive — coverage may start three months after your arrival date in British Columbia (the balance of the month in which you establish residence, plus two months). Because of that wait period, the Province advises you get private health care insurance to cover the gap; UBC's schedule notes that if you arrived in August, your waiting period will likely be over in November. MSP premiums are $0 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents and $75/month for students on a study permit. Apply online (the easiest and fastest way), in person or by mail; completing enrolment gets you a Personal Health Number (PHN) via the B.C. Services Card process. Note: coverage depends on residency — if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses. The sources provided do not name the specific UBC office that handles MSP enrolment for graduate students, so confirm that directly with UBC.
prerequisites: Arrival in British Columbia (the 3-month wait period starts from your arrival date)
ID documents meeting MSP's ID requirements
Private health insurance arranged to cover the wait period before MSP coverage begins
steps.cost: $0/month for Canadian citizens and permanent residents; $75/month for students on a study permit (plus the cost of private interim coverage during the wait period)
steps.time_estimate: Apply as soon as you arrive; coverage may start about three months after your arrival date in B.C.

steps.title: Check your MSP application status and plan for the 3-month wait period
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP) to access provincial health benefits like doctor visits. If you're new to Canada, coverage may only start three months after your arrival date in B.C. — the wait period is the balance of the month in which you establish residence plus two months. Confirming your application is progressing and knowing your exact coverage start date tells you how long you must carry private health insurance, which the Province advises you to get while you wait. Note that coverage depends on residency: if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses. Family members who arrive later must keep their existing coverage and are added separately, with each person's wait period starting on their own arrival date. If you already have MSP and received a letter to renew your B.C. Services Card, don't submit a new application — just follow the renewal instructions in the letter.
prerequisites: MSP Application for Enrolment already submitted (online, in person or by mail)
Your arrival date in British Columbia, to calculate the wait period
Application/confirmation reference or ID documents used when applying
If your coverage will be under an employer, union or pension group plan, your group administrator's contact details
steps.cost: No fee to apply for or enrol in MSP; you should budget for private health insurance to cover the wait period
steps.time_estimate: 15–30 minutes to check status and confirm your coverage start date
